title: Objectwise weak equivalences of enriched Kan diagrams transpose to coherent equivalences
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. Use enriched categories, the coherent realization/nerve adjunction, and $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $J$ be a small simplicial set and $F,G:\mathfrak C[J]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$ enriched functors. Let $\varphi:F\to G$ be an enriched natural transformation whose components $\varphi_j:F(j)\to G(j)$ are weak homotopy equivalences. Write $m_F,m_G:J\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ for the transposes. Regard $\varphi$ as an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[J]\times\mathfrak C[\Delta^1]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}$; precompose with the enriched functor $\mathfrak C[J\times\Delta^1]\to\mathfrak C[J]\times\mathfrak C[\Delta^1]$ induced by the two projections, and transpose. The resulting coherent transformation $m_F\to m_G$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$, and its component at $j$ is the edge represented by $\varphi_j$. For any weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes $f:X\to Y$, the edge represented by $f$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ is an equivalence. Both assertions allow empty Kan complexes and are natural under restriction of $J$.

source.place: Returned Step 14, passage from enriched weak equivalence to coherent equivalence; HTT 1.1.5 and 2.2.5 Argument extracted from the returned proof; HTT supplies the background constructions, not a verbatim assertion of this formulated lemma. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison.

proof.text: Let \(\psi:\mathfrak C[J\times\Delta^1]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\) be the composite of the enriched functor representing \(\varphi\), \(\mathfrak C[J]\times\mathfrak C[\Delta^1]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\), with the enriched functor \((\mathfrak C[\mathrm{pr}_1],\mathfrak C[\mathrm{pr}_2])\) induced by the two projections. Here \(\mathfrak C[\Delta^1]\) has objects \(0,1\) and the single vertex \(\{0,1\}\) in its mapping set from \(0\) to \(1\), so the functor representing \(\varphi\) is \(F\) on \(\mathfrak C[J]\times\{0\}\), \(G\) on \(\mathfrak C[J]\times\{1\}\), and sends \((a,\{0,1\})\) for \(a\in\mathfrak C[J](j,j')\) to \(\varphi_{j'}\circ F(a)=G(a)\circ\varphi_j\). Since \(\mathfrak C[K]\) is the colimit of the \(\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\) over the simplices of \(K\) and \(N_{\mathrm{hc}}\) has \(n\)-simplices the enriched functors out of \(\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\), enriched functors \(\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\) correspond to simplicial maps \(K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}\), naturally in \(K\) (the stipulated coherent-realization/coherent-nerve adjunction). Thus \(\psi\) transposes to \(\tau:J\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}\), and for \(i:K\to J\times\Delta^1\) the restriction \(\tau\circ i\) is the transpose of \(\psi\circ\mathfrak C[i]\). For \(i:J\cong J\times\{0\}\subset J\times\Delta^1\) the composite \((\mathfrak C[\mathrm{pr}_1],\mathfrak C[\mathrm{pr}_2])\circ\mathfrak C[i]\) is \((\mathrm{id},\text{const}_0)\), so \(\tau|_{J\times\{0\}}\) is the transpose \(m_F\) of \(F\); likewise \(\tau|_{J\times\{1\}}=m_G\). For \(i:\Delta^1\cong\{j\}\times\Delta^1\) the composite is \((\text{const}_j,\mathrm{id})\), so the edge \(\tau|_{\{j\}\times\Delta^1}\) is the enriched functor \(\mathfrak C[\Delta^1]\to\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\) with objects \(F(j),G(j)\) and vertex \(\varphi_j\in\operatorname{Fun}(F(j),G(j))_0\), i.e. the edge represented by \(\varphi_j\). The coherent-nerve convention is postcomposition in every degree, so this construction retains all higher simplicial parameters and restrictions.

source.place: HTT §§1.1.5 and 2.2.5, coherent-realization/coherent-nerve adjunction and naturality; returned Step 14 transposition construction

proof.text: Let \(f:X\to Y\) be any weak homotopy equivalence of \(\mathcal V\)-small Kan complexes (objects of \(\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}\)); by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] this means its realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group at every basepoint of \(|X|\), which is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse]. That lemma gives a simplicial map \(g:Y\to X\) and simplicial maps \(H:X\times\Delta^1\to X\), \(K:Y\times\Delta^1\to Y\) with \(H|_{X\times\{0\}}=gf\), \(H|_{X\times\{1\}}=1_X\), \(K|_{Y\times\{0\}}=fg\), \(K|_{Y\times\{1\}}=1_Y\); its statement explicitly allows empty and disconnected Kan complexes. These are simplicial homotopies between \(gf\) and \(1_X\) and between \(fg\) and \(1_Y\) in the sense of [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-inverse-equivalence], which then gives the two inverse-triangle \(2\)-simplices in \(\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}\) with boundaries \((f,g,1_X)\) and \((g,f,1_Y)\); hence the edge represented by \(f\), namely its vertex of \(\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)\), is an equivalence edge. This is the second assertion, including empty \(X,Y\) (then \(X=Y=\varnothing\), since \(f\) is bijective on components). For every vertex \(j\in J_0\), the hypothesis says that \(\varphi_j:F(j)\to G(j)\) is a weak homotopy equivalence of \(\mathcal V\)-small Kan complexes, so the edge represented by \(\varphi_j\), which is the component \(\tau|_{\{j\}\times\Delta^1}\) by Step 1, is an equivalence.

source.place: Kerodon 4.6.7.7 and 4.6.8, through the existing Kan weak-equivalence edge lemma

proof.text: The simplicial category \(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\) has Kan mapping simplicial sets, so \(\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal V}\) is a quasicategory. Apply the pointwise criterion [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] to the edge \(\tau:m_F\to m_G\) of \(\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})\). Since all its vertex components are equivalence edges by Step 2, \(\tau\) is an equivalence in the functor quasicategory.

source.place: Kerodon Theorem 4.4.4.4, pointwise equivalence criterion; coherent-nerve quasicategory criterion

proof.text: Every simplicial map \(u:J'\to J\) restricts the construction in Step 1 by precomposition with \(u\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}\); the endpoint diagrams and component edges are the corresponding restrictions. The same inverse triangles from Step 2 and the pointwise criterion from Step 3 therefore commute with restriction, proving the asserted naturality under restriction of \(J\).

source.place: Naturality of the coherent-nerve adjunction under restriction; elementary functoriality

proof_origin.place: HTT §§1.1.5 and 2.2.5; returned Step 14 passage from an enriched objectwise weak equivalence to a coherent equivalence
